sentence: This project provides statistical and bioinformatics services that help cancer researchers with study design, data analysis and review of clinical trials.
This project uses genomics and computational biology methods to find the genes and pathways that contribute to alcohol use disorder in different brain regions.
This project provides vision researchers with shared imaging, animal models and sequencing, mass spectroscopy and proteomics facilities.
This project studies how antibiotic changes to the gut microbiota affect the gut lining and the inflammation of the joint in arthritis.
This project tries to find out how the interplay between SARS-CoV-2 and host factors controls viral gene expression.
This project tries to find out how macrophages transfer mitochondria to cancer cells and how this process is regulated during metastasis.
This project studies a unique subtype of natural killer cells that can recruit anti-tumor immune cells and survive in tumor environments.
This project develops a way to detect early cognitive decline in older adults by assessing their mood, stress and thinking in daily life.
This project tests whether a tumor DNA assay combined with protein-based MRI can accurately identify when glioblastoma returns after therapy.
This project analyzes biospecimens from immunotherapy clinical trials to learn the mechanisms behind how cancer patients respond to immune-based therapies.
This project develops deep learning methods that design peptides and macrocycles able to bind disease-relevant protein targets.
This project builds genomics and biomedical informatics expertise to support translational research that addresses health disparities in communities.
This project studies how physical and soluble factors around cartilage cells lead to cartilage loss with aging and according to sex.
This project uses high-throughput screening to find non-nicotine compounds in electronic nicotine delivery systems that act on nicotinic receptors.
This project builds a catalog of cellular programs by combining CRISPR, single-cell, imaging and human genetics data to identify genes behind human disease.
This project studies how glutamine metabolism may help breast cancer spread to bone and whether existing therapies targeting it could reduce bone metastasis.
This project offers mass spectrometry analysis of proteins and support with experimental design and data analysis to cancer researchers.
This project studies how variants in a calcium channel gene affect interneuron migration and neurodevelopment using human-derived neural organoids and assembloids.
This project uses protein engineering to study and modify human antimicrobial peptides as a basis for developing antibiotics.
This project tries to find out how a secreted phospholipase controls immune responses in the airways of people with asthma.
